method: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Boy N, Mühlhausen C, Maier EM, et al., Journal of Inherited Metabolic Disease (SSIEM/Wiley) 'Recommendations for diagnosing and managing individuals with glutaric aciduria type 1: Third revision' (vol. 46, pp. 482–519, published 2023 (online November 2022)). Every claim is a paraphrase backed by anchors (scripts/anchor.py): verify.py --source re-finds each anchored span in a fresh copy of the source, checks the claim's numbers against it and rejects copying. LICENCE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (read at the article's own licence line ('open access article under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivs License') in the publisher PDF, retrieved from the Leipzig University repository (ul.qucosa.de, found via Unpaywall); Unpaywall lists cc-by-nc-nd for the version of record). The source's words are NOT reproduced here. Text extracted with pdftotext in reading order (not -layout), because the two-column layout otherwise interleaves columns mid-sentence. The Zurich repository copy (ZORA) sat behind an Anubis bot challenge and was not used. Table text that pdftotext interleaves into the body (Tables 4 and 5, emergency regimens) was not anchored.

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Most untreated children suffer an acute striatal injury before age 3 (to 6) years,** set off by infection, fever or surgery, leaving a permanent, mainly dystonic movement disorder.
claims.locator: Boy N, Mühlhausen C, Maier EM, et al., Journal of Inherited Metabolic Disease (SSIEM/Wiley), 'Recommendations for diagnosing and managing individuals with glutaric aciduria type 1: Third revision', vol. 46, pp. 482–519, published 2023 (online November 2022), https://doi.org/10.1002/jimd.12566, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Confirm an abnormal newborn screen or suggestive findings** by measuring glutaric and 3-hydroxyglutaric acid in urine and/or blood, then, if abnormal, GCDH gene or enzyme testing. (strong)
claims.locator: Boy N, Mühlhausen C, Maier EM, et al., Journal of Inherited Metabolic Disease (SSIEM/Wiley), 'Recommendations for diagnosing and managing individuals with glutaric aciduria type 1: Third revision', vol. 46, pp. 482–519, published 2023 (online November 2022), https://doi.org/10.1002/jimd.12566, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Subdural haematoma or hygroma together with frontotemporal hypoplasia and widened anterior temporal CSF spaces warrants targeted testing for GA1.** (strong)
claims.locator: Boy N, Mühlhausen C, Maier EM, et al., Journal of Inherited Metabolic Disease (SSIEM/Wiley), 'Recommendations for diagnosing and managing individuals with glutaric aciduria type 1: Third revision', vol. 46, pp. 482–519, published 2023 (online November 2022), https://doi.org/10.1002/jimd.12566, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Work-up, treatment planning and family training belong in a specialised metabolic centre;** transfer patients diagnosed elsewhere promptly. (strong)
claims.locator: Boy N, Mühlhausen C, Maier EM, et al., Journal of Inherited Metabolic Disease (SSIEM/Wiley), 'Recommendations for diagnosing and managing individuals with glutaric aciduria type 1: Third revision', vol. 46, pp. 482–519, published 2023 (online November 2022), https://doi.org/10.1002/jimd.12566, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Low-lysine diet for every patient until 6 years of age, with a lysine-free, tryptophan-reduced, arginine-enriched amino acid mixture to cover protein needs.** (strong)
claims.locator: Boy N, Mühlhausen C, Maier EM, et al., Journal of Inherited Metabolic Disease (SSIEM/Wiley), 'Recommendations for diagnosing and managing individuals with glutaric aciduria type 1: Third revision', vol. 46, pp. 482–519, published 2023 (online November 2022), https://doi.org/10.1002/jimd.12566, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **After 6 years, move to an age-adapted, protein-controlled diet** built on safe protein intakes that limits high-lysine foods, with regular dietetic support through the change.
claims.locator: Boy N, Mühlhausen C, Maier EM, et al., Journal of Inherited Metabolic Disease (SSIEM/Wiley), 'Recommendations for diagnosing and managing individuals with glutaric aciduria type 1: Third revision', vol. 46, pp. 482–519, published 2023 (online November 2022), https://doi.org/10.1002/jimd.12566, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Extra single-amino-acid arginine is not recommended** beyond what food and the amino acid mixture provide; no clinical benefit has been shown.
claims.locator: Boy N, Mühlhausen C, Maier EM, et al., Journal of Inherited Metabolic Disease (SSIEM/Wiley), 'Recommendations for diagnosing and managing individuals with glutaric aciduria type 1: Third revision', vol. 46, pp. 482–519, published 2023 (online November 2022), https://doi.org/10.1002/jimd.12566, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Give carnitine for life,** keeping the free carnitine level (plasma or blood spot) within normal limits.
claims.locator: Boy N, Mühlhausen C, Maier EM, et al., Journal of Inherited Metabolic Disease (SSIEM/Wiley), 'Recommendations for diagnosing and managing individuals with glutaric aciduria type 1: Third revision', vol. 46, pp. 482–519, published 2023 (online November 2022), https://doi.org/10.1002/jimd.12566, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Vaccinate on the national schedule.**
claims.locator: Boy N, Mühlhausen C, Maier EM, et al., Journal of Inherited Metabolic Disease (SSIEM/Wiley), 'Recommendations for diagnosing and managing individuals with glutaric aciduria type 1: Third revision', vol. 46, pp. 482–519, published 2023 (online November 2022), https://doi.org/10.1002/jimd.12566, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Up to age 6, start emergency treatment at once, and intensively, for any febrile illness, alarming symptom or surgery.** (strong; very high clinical relevance)
claims.locator: Boy N, Mühlhausen C, Maier EM, et al., Journal of Inherited Metabolic Disease (SSIEM/Wiley), 'Recommendations for diagnosing and managing individuals with glutaric aciduria type 1: Third revision', vol. 46, pp. 482–519, published 2023 (online November 2022), https://doi.org/10.1002/jimd.12566, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Home emergency treatment is possible only if the child is clinically well despite fever.**
claims.locator: Boy N, Mühlhausen C, Maier EM, et al., Journal of Inherited Metabolic Disease (SSIEM/Wiley), 'Recommendations for diagnosing and managing individuals with glutaric aciduria type 1: Third revision', vol. 46, pp. 482–519, published 2023 (online November 2022), https://doi.org/10.1002/jimd.12566, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Transfer without delay to the metabolic centre (or the nearest hospital under its supervision) for IV treatment** if there is recurrent vomiting or diarrhoea, poor feed tolerance, high fever or any suspicious neurological sign.
claims.locator: Boy N, Mühlhausen C, Maier EM, et al., Journal of Inherited Metabolic Disease (SSIEM/Wiley), 'Recommendations for diagnosing and managing individuals with glutaric aciduria type 1: Third revision', vol. 46, pp. 482–519, published 2023 (online November 2022), https://doi.org/10.1002/jimd.12566, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **After 6 years, emergency treatment can still be used for severe illness or surgery,** adapting glucose and fluids to the individual; crises have not been reported at this age, but silent damage cannot be excluded.
claims.locator: Boy N, Mühlhausen C, Maier EM, et al., Journal of Inherited Metabolic Disease (SSIEM/Wiley), 'Recommendations for diagnosing and managing individuals with glutaric aciduria type 1: Third revision', vol. 46, pp. 482–519, published 2023 (online November 2022), https://doi.org/10.1002/jimd.12566, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Movement disorder, seizures and subdural collections are managed by a neuropaediatrician or neurologist and/or neurosurgeon working closely with the metabolic team.**
claims.locator: Boy N, Mühlhausen C, Maier EM, et al., Journal of Inherited Metabolic Disease (SSIEM/Wiley), 'Recommendations for diagnosing and managing individuals with glutaric aciduria type 1: Third revision', vol. 46, pp. 482–519, published 2023 (online November 2022), https://doi.org/10.1002/jimd.12566, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **In the first 3 years, admit and observe for at least 24 h after even a minor head injury,** because of the subdural haematoma risk.
claims.locator: Boy N, Mühlhausen C, Maier EM, et al., Journal of Inherited Metabolic Disease (SSIEM/Wiley), 'Recommendations for diagnosing and managing individuals with glutaric aciduria type 1: Third revision', vol. 46, pp. 482–519, published 2023 (online November 2022), https://doi.org/10.1002/jimd.12566, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Image the brain at any age if neurological symptoms appear or clearly worsen;** routine MRI for extrastriatal changes may start from 10 years, for example every 2–5 years.
claims.locator: Boy N, Mühlhausen C, Maier EM, et al., Journal of Inherited Metabolic Disease (SSIEM/Wiley), 'Recommendations for diagnosing and managing individuals with glutaric aciduria type 1: Third revision', vol. 46, pp. 482–519, published 2023 (online November 2022), https://doi.org/10.1002/jimd.12566, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Do not use urine glutaric or 3-hydroxyglutaric acid levels to monitor or adjust treatment.**
claims.locator: Boy N, Mühlhausen C, Maier EM, et al., Journal of Inherited Metabolic Disease (SSIEM/Wiley), 'Recommendations for diagnosing and managing individuals with glutaric aciduria type 1: Third revision', vol. 46, pp. 482–519, published 2023 (online November 2022), https://doi.org/10.1002/jimd.12566, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **On the low-lysine diet, check plasma amino acids regularly, 3–4 h after a meal, keeping them in the age-specific normal range;** keep trough free carnitine (at least 12 h after the last dose) in range.
claims.locator: Boy N, Mühlhausen C, Maier EM, et al., Journal of Inherited Metabolic Disease (SSIEM/Wiley), 'Recommendations for diagnosing and managing individuals with glutaric aciduria type 1: Third revision', vol. 46, pp. 482–519, published 2023 (online November 2022), https://doi.org/10.1002/jimd.12566, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Check kidney function every year from 6 years of age;** assess IQ or developmental quotient, motor function and language regularly.
claims.locator: Boy N, Mühlhausen C, Maier EM, et al., Journal of Inherited Metabolic Disease (SSIEM/Wiley), 'Recommendations for diagnosing and managing individuals with glutaric aciduria type 1: Third revision', vol. 46, pp. 482–519, published 2023 (online November 2022), https://doi.org/10.1002/jimd.12566, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Plan a structured move to adult care starting from 14 years of age,** with regular age-appropriate education and quality-of-life review by an interdisciplinary team.
claims.locator: Boy N, Mühlhausen C, Maier EM, et al., Journal of Inherited Metabolic Disease (SSIEM/Wiley), 'Recommendations for diagnosing and managing individuals with glutaric aciduria type 1: Third revision', vol. 46, pp. 482–519, published 2023 (online November 2022), https://doi.org/10.1002/jimd.12566, retrieved 2026-09-23
